A non-relocating parent has legal rights that may allow them to challenge a child's proposed move, request a custody hearing, and seek changes to an existing parenting arrangement. When one parent plans to move to another city or state with the child, the other parent does not necessarily lose their say in the decision. Courts often evaluate relocation disputes using the best interests of the child standard , considering how the move could affect the child's well-being. A move-away lawyer can help the non-relocating parent understand their legal options and take appropriate steps to protect their parental rights. articles.title: AI Is Changing Mental Health Care
articles.author: Tiqua Jackson
articles.content_excerpt: The opinions expressed here are solely the author's and do not reflect the opinions or beliefs of the LA Progressive. Artificial intelligence is finding its way into mental health care, changing how people seek help, receive diagnoses, and connect with treatment providers. What once required a phone call or an office visit can now begin with a chatbot, an online questionnaire, or an automated screening tool. For people who have spent weeks trying to find a therapist, that sounds like progress. But the growing use of AI in mental health services is also raising concerns about patient safety, privacy, and the loss of human connection. articles.title: Members Alarmed by End-Run around Democracy at Buffalo Health Care Local
articles.author: Sarah Hughes
articles.content_excerpt: Things had been tense for some time inside the leadership of Communications Workers (CWA) Local 1168, a 4,800-member health care union based near Buffalo, New York. Still, it was a high-functioning local with a busy calendar of events, stewards handling grievances, organizers pursuing leads, and leaders organizing at work. So it was a surprise to members in June when their parent union, CWA, put the local into trusteeship, at the request of the local’s president and seven of the nineteen executive board members. Trusteeship meant the union’s bylaws and elected leaders were suspended, and most of its work temporarily ground to a halt. articles.title: Election Denial Is Now Normal for the Right Everywhere
articles.author: Branko Marcetic
articles.content_excerpt: The series of recent elections across the globe have been read as a stinging defeat for right-wing authoritarians, which they are. But maybe more notable is another element: that denial of and efforts to simply reverse unfavorable election results now seem to have become de rigueur for the transnational Right. All four of the major elections taking place in the ten-day period from October 25 to November 3 have seen or are seeing efforts by right-wing politicians to cast doubt on results where they lost or are likely to, and to engineer a way to change them in their favor. articles.title: Bottom-Up Organizing: How We Got Clean Porta-Johns
articles.content_excerpt: The first day I showed up on the Marriott construction site in downtown Detroit, everyone warned me about the state of our bathrooms. You could smell them halfway across most floors. They were full in 24 hours, urinals were often clogged, and some people had taken to using buckets and hiding them in closets. Every electrician already had the same idea: we wanted the cleaning schedule changed from twice a week to three times. I had a long conversation with the steward about what had been tried. The first instinct of a construction worker is to “drag” (quit), drive over to the union hall, and pick up a new job. articles.title: Is There Life After AI? Cory Doctorow Thinks So.
articles.author: Cory Doctorow
articles.content_excerpt: The artificial intelligence boom is fueled by an elite wager that software can supplant expensive human expertise. The tech industry and its investors are pumping hundreds of billions of dollars into the technology — Goldman Sachs forecasts that global AI-related investment will soon exceed $1 trillion . At the same time, government regulatory regimes are inadequate and consumer use cases often vague, misleading, or utterly counterproductive. The economics of AI don’t make sense unless one factors in what its backers hope to gain: a way to displace workers. In his most recent book, The Reverse Centaur’s Guide to Life After AI , Cory Doctorow explains how people have become tools of the machines and the capitalists who own them. In the past, many Palestinians and Arabs followed Israeli elections closely. They did so not because they entertained illusions that a Zionist leader would deliver peace and justice, dismantle the occupation or remove illegal settlements. Rather, they feared that some Israeli leaders were worse than others. They hoped to avert the worst-case scenario. Over time, however, that distinction gave way to the belief that all Israeli leaders were essentially the same. This is not pessimism. It is experience.
